problem_statement: This is the AI Code Translator workspace (mckaywrigley/ai-code-translator, a Next.js 13 pages-router app): it converts a code snippet from one language into another with CodeMirror editors, a language pair, a GPT-3.5/GPT-4 model select, and a violet Translate button. Add the app's own "Snippet library" — a browser of the built-in starter translation snippets that lives in the workspace beneath the toolbar AND on a dedicated /library route. The library shows an eyebrow "Snippet library" (class snippet-library__eyebrow), a title "Load a starter snippet to translate", a category tab bar (class snippet-tabs) with buttons All / Algorithms / Web / Data / Scripting (class snippet-tab), a live readout (#snippet-readout) that starts at "Showing all 8 snippets", and a grid (class snippet-grid) of eight snippet cards (class snippet-card) — each with a name (h3), a language-pair (from → to), a category chip, and a one-line blurb. Register a "Snippet library" destination in the shared header nav (components/navLinks.ts) so the same a.nav-link renders on the workspace, the /library catalog, and the /guide page. The tab bar filters the cards and the readout re-reads the visible count on every click ("Showing 2 · Data"); on a 390px phone the tab bar and card grid must WRAP so the workspace never scrolls sideways; and every card must render legible light-on-dark text with a readable violet language chip on desktop, tablet, and mobile. Keep the translator behaviour (key input, model select, language selects, Translate) unchanged.
required_content: A native Snippet library (class snippet-library) is rendered in the workspace beneath the toolbar and on a dedicated /library route, with the same eyebrow "Snippet library", title, category tab bar (All / Algorithms / Web / Data / Scripting), #snippet-readout starting "Showing all 8 snippets", and a grid of eight snippet-card items.
A "Snippet library" destination is registered in the shared header nav (components/navLinks.ts) so the same a.nav-link renders across the workspace, /library, and /guide routes.
Clicking a category tab filters the cards AND re-reads the live count into #snippet-readout (e.g. "Showing 2 · Data"); clicking All restores "Showing all 8 snippets".

On a 390px mobile viewport the snippet tab bar and card grid wrap so the workspace has no horizontal overflow beyond a small tolerance; on 834px tablet and 1440px desktop the library lays out cleanly with no overflow.
Every snippet card renders legible light-on-dark text with a readable language-pair and category chip at every viewport (no dark-on-dark or overlapping/clipped cards).

The title, API-key input, model select, Translate button, status line, language selects, and code editors remain present and unchanged; no new console errors or failed network requests are introduced.

The rendered screenshots of the workspace and /library visual states must show the snippet cards as legible light-on-dark assets (readable card name, language-pair, and category chip) — a card grid that renders dark-on-dark or overlapping is a visual-state regression even if the card text is present in the DOM.
design_constraints: Preserve the app's design language: dark #0E1117 background, neutral-200 text, violet accents, #1F2937 controls, and the existing vertical workspace layout order.
The Snippet library must be the app's own native browsing surface (a category-filtered snippet browser with cards and a live readout), not a bolted-on metric-tile strip.
Fit 390px mobile, 834px tablet, and 1440px desktop; the tab bar and card grid must wrap on mobile and must not depend on hiding overflow at the body/html level or clipping content off-screen.
Render the same Snippet library on the /library catalog route and register the nav destination once in components/navLinks.ts so the header is consistent across routes.
Keep the Next.js build pipeline intact — `next build` must still emit a working app that serves with `next start`.
state_constraints: desktop_home / desktop_home_library capture the workspace at 1440px with the Snippet library, tab bar (All active), readout "Showing all 8 snippets", and eight legible cards, no overflow.
mobile_home / mobile_home_library capture the 390px workspace: the tab bar and card grid wrap so the document does not overflow horizontally beyond tolerance.
tablet_home captures the workspace at 834px with no overflow.
desktop_filter_data clicks the Data category tab; the grid filters to the two Data snippets and #snippet-readout re-reads to "Showing 2 · Data" (changed from desktop_home_library).
desktop_library / mobile_library / tablet_library capture the dedicated /library catalog route with the same Snippet library and the shared "Snippet library" nav-link.
desktop_library_filter_web clicks the Web tab on /library and reads "Showing 2 · Web".
desktop_guide captures the /guide route, confirming the shared nav (including the Snippet library link) renders on a third route.
desktop_translate fills a key and code and runs the offline canned translation to confirm the translator flow is unchanged with no external network.

change_completion: The Snippet library renders in the workspace and on /library with the eyebrow, title, tab bar, #snippet-readout, and eight snippet cards.
Clicking a category tab filters the cards and updates the live readout to "Showing N · Category".
The "Snippet library" nav-link is registered and renders on every route.
design_consistency: The library preserves the dark translator identity and violet accent, and the same library appears on the workspace and the /library catalog.
Snippet cards are legible light-on-dark with readable language and category chips — no dark-on-dark, overlap, or clipping.
responsive: On a 390px mobile viewport the snippet tab bar and card grid wrap so the document width stays within the viewport (no horizontal overflow / no sideways scroll).
On 834px tablet and 1440px desktop viewports the library lays out cleanly with no horizontal overflow and the cards stay legible.
regression: No visual or behavioural regression: the title, API-key input, model select, Translate button, status line, language selects, and CodeMirror editors stay present, unchanged, and in the same layout order.
No new console errors or failed network requests are introduced, and the offline translate flow still runs unchanged.

author_notes: Repo-grounded add/design_continuity task on the Next.js 13 pages-router mckaywrigley ai-code-translator workspace app (ai_chat_app). The native lever is the app's OWN Snippet library: a category-filtered browser of the built-in starter translation snippets (snippet-card cards showing name, language pair, category chip, blurb) hosted in the translator workspace and repeated on a dedicated /library catalog route, plus a shared header nav registered once in components/navLinks.ts. This is a genuine translator feature (a snippet/preset library), NOT a metric-tile rail. The app is offline INFRA (identical across legs): next/font/google Inter is a local system-font stack and the remote OpenAI stream in utils/index.ts is a local canned-response ReadableStream, so no external request or API key is needed. Four orthogonal gates discriminate: D6 no_horizontal_overflow (tol 24) on mobile/tablet home; D3 visual_regression on the home library states (snippet cards / heading crops); D2 cross-route dom_assertions (the shared a.nav-link 'Snippet library' and the snippet-library / snippet-card structure on /library); D4 interaction_assertions (the category tab filters the cards and the live #snippet-readout re-reads the count). reference passes all four; baseline reproduces the fixed-width non-wrapping layout defect (fails D6+D3+D2, still filters correctly so passes D4); bad is a smart-wrong solution failing all four. Design keywords: snippet library, category filter, language pair, dark workspace, legible cards, responsive wrap.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: mckaywrigley/ai-code-translator is a runnable Next.js 13 pages-router code-translation workspace; its natural feature surface (a browsable library of starter translation snippets with a category filter and a live count, repeated on a catalog route and reachable from a shared header nav) is an ideal native host for an add/design_continuity task graded by four orthogonal gates (mobile overflow, card legibility/visual fidelity, cross-route consistency, and the live filter interaction). The app is offline/network-clean INFRA identical across legs.
